d: A hypothalamic peptide that stimulates GnRH neurons and helps restart pulsatile GnRH at puberty. Activating mutations of its receptor cause central precocious puberty; inactivating mutations block puberty.
Maturation of the adrenal zona reticularis in mid-childhood. Under ACTH it makes DHEA and DHEA-S, which cause pubic and axillary hair, body odor and acne without any gonadal activity.
Skeletal maturity read from an X-ray of the left hand and wrist. Sex steroids advance it, so it runs ahead in precocious puberty and behind in constitutional delay and hypogonadism.
A benign mass of hypothalamic tissue that contains its own GnRH neurons. It is the classic brain lesion behind central precocious puberty in young boys and can cause laughing (gelastic) seizures.

A postzygotic activating GNAS mutation that keeps Gs signaling on in scattered cells. It causes peripheral precocious puberty from autonomous ovarian cysts, café-au-lait macules and polyostotic fibrous dysplasia.

t: Constitutional delay of growth and puberty
d: The most common cause of late puberty: a healthy, short child with a delayed bone age, often with a late-maturing parent. Puberty eventually starts on its own.
Familial male-limited precocious puberty from an activating LH receptor mutation. Leydig cells make testosterone without LH, so a young boy virilizes with a low LH and modestly enlarged testes.
